author: Connor Nielsen
title: Lawton hosts PACT Act disability benefits event - NewsBreak
text:
By Connor Nielsen ,
13 hours ago
LAWTON ( KFDX/KJTL ) — Veterans of Oklahoma are invited to get support and learn about their benefits at a disability claims event in Lawton.
The Lawton Indian Health Service and VA will host a PACT Act disability presumptive conditions event on Wednesday, September 23, from 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. at the Lawton Farmers Market Building, located at 77 SW 4th St .
The event, "Your Service. Our Mission: Bringing VA Benefits Home," will focus on helping veterans, their spouses and all surviving spouses across the state who may have presumptive disabilities and are eligible for a VA pension claim or health care.
Presumptive disabilities are conditions the VA presumes to be related to military service, even if they develop after being discharged and can qualify for compensation. Spouses and widows are encouraged to attend, as they can be eligible for Dependency and Indemnity Compensation if a veteran has passed away from a presumptive condition.
Under the PACT Act, VA health care and benefits expand for those exposed to burn pits, Agent Orange and other toxic substances during their military service.
Attendees will get help from Veterans Service Officers to complete VA disability claim paperwork and will also receive onsite Compensation and Pension exams in select scenarios. Not all claims can be provided; the service is being offered wherever possible.
VA staff will offer toxic exposure screenings and supply ID card replacements for expired cards.
Many representatives from the Oklahoma City VA Health Care System, Muskogee VA Regional Office, Oklahoma Department of Veterans Affairs, local Vet Centers, Tribal and Indian Health Service programs, Tribal Veteran Service Officers, and various nonprofit partners will be onsite to answer questions.
Veterans attending, if available, are asked to bring:
Medical records/medical evidence (such as doctor or hospital records) Documents that provide historical or military information relevant to the disability being claimed Discharge or separation papers (DD-214 or equivalent) Widow/dependent records (such as marriage certificate, death certificate, children's birth certificate VA continues its nationwide outreach campaign to make a meaningful impact on the lives of veterans, spouses and widows of veterans who have been previously unreached.
